subject: Retention windows for ephemeral prompts and backups — evidence request

Subject: Request: retention specifics for logs/backups and prompt handling (SOC2/SIG evidence)

Hi Soojin —

As part of our SIG review (we're validating for a HIT-regulated workload), the security team needs a concise summary and supporting artifacts for the following items:

- Retention windows for server/app logs (auth, request, error) and the policy for immutable backups/snapshots.
- Deletion lifecycle for backups (scheduled deletions, retention tiers, geo-redundant copies).
- Handling of model prompts and responses that may contain PHI/PII: are prompts persisted? retention TTLs? scrub/overwrite procedures?
- Evidence: SOC2 report, retention runbook or SOP, and any automated deletion job logs we can redact.

Can you send the above or point us to short artifacts (PDF/MD) we can upload to our SIG intake? Ideally we have something by COB tomorrow.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Security Analyst — Acme Health

Subject: Re: Request: retention specifics for logs/backups and prompt handling (SOC2/SIG evidence)

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front:

- Application and auth logs: default retention 90 days hot, 12 months archived (encrypted), deletions performed by periodic lifecycle job; immutable snapshots kept for compliance retention windows and then pruned according to retention tier.
- Backups/snapshots: daily snapshots retained 30 days; weekly snapshots retained 12 weeks; monthly snapshots retained 12 months for committed customers (can be configured shorter for hosted). Geo-redundant copies exist in a second region; deletion is coordinated by unique snapshot id and audited.
- Prompt retention: by default we persist prompts + responses for 30 days for quality monitoring and troubleshooting; for customers who opt-out we can set prompt retention to 0 (ephemeral mode) and disable storage of prompt text. When stored, prompts are encrypted at rest and redaction/scrubbing is supported via a configurable pipeline.

I can attach SOC2 Type II and our retention runbook, and Marcus will add the backup retention artifact. Priya will add a short note on contractual language for DPA/SCC alignment.

I'll attach what we have and follow up with the automated deletion job logs (redacted).

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Compliance Operations

Subject: Re: Request: retention specifics for logs/backups and prompt handling (SOC2/SIG evidence)

Adding technical detail from infra:

- Backup retention policy is implemented in the snapshot manager (k8s-controller + object lifecycle). Each snapshot record contains: snapshot_id, creation_ts, retention_tier, replicas, and deletion_ts. Deletion is executed by the retention-worker which marks objects for deletion and then performs a secure wipe (S3 object overwrite with zeroes before tombstone) for eligible customers under stricter regs.
- Log retention: logs flow to our write-ahead aggregator; hot indices are retained on SSDs for 90d. Cold indices moved to encrypted object storage with 12mo TTL. We keep audit trails for deletion operations for 3 years per SOC2.
- Prompt retention & scrubbing: if customer opts into prompt collection, prompts are stored in a separate encrypted store with a TTL tag. We support TTL=0 (no persistence), TTL=30d (default), or custom TTL up to 2 years under contract. Scrubbing pipeline: regex-based PII masking, then manual review escalation for matches above a threshold (alerting to customer-configured webhook).

Attachment: backup-snapshot-policy-2026.png (diagram).

-Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Backup deletion timelines and evidence: we will provide a redacted deletion runbook and execution logs showing snapshot IDs and deletion timestamps; we can append a page to the runbook that maps the data lifecycle to contractual obligations (SCC/DPA clauses).

Soojin —

Received, thanks for the quick turnaround. We'll review the runbook and SOC2 PDF and get back if we need the deletion job exports. Two quick clarifications before I close the intake:

1) For the TTL=0 opt-out, does that also disable transient in-memory caching entirely (i.e., no KV cache persisted to disk)?
2) Can you confirm whether secondary geo-replicas are deleted in the same job or require separate replication cleanup (we need proof of end-to-end deletion across replicas).

If you can confirm those two items in one line each, that would be perfect. Otherwise we'll open a follow-up.

Appreciate it —
Liam
